items.prompt: A right-angled triangle has legs 9 and 12. Calculate the length of the hypotenuse.

points.text: Squares both legs to reach 81 and 144 as the two squared lengths
Adds the squares to 225 and takes the square root to give hypotenuse 15

items.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 17 and one leg 8. Calculate the length of the other leg.

points.text: Subtracts the known square from the hypotenuse square as 289 minus 64
Takes the square root of 225 to give the other leg as 15

items.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, angle theta has opposite side 5 and hypotenuse 13. Write down sin theta and cos theta.

points.text: Writes sin theta as opposite over hypotenuse giving five thirteenths
Writes cos theta as adjacent over hypotenuse giving twelve thirteenths

items.prompt: Explain how the sine rule can find an unknown side in a triangle that has no right angle.

points.text: States the sine rule pairing each side with the sine of its opposite angle
Describes substituting a known side-angle pair and the target angle to solve for the unknown side

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Working is sequenced so each squaring, ratio or rule choice is justified before the answer.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Method is broadly sound but slips appear that the written working still makes traceable.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Steps are disconnected and the chosen method cannot be followed from the working shown.
